editorial:
Imagine you are stepping onto a fancy old train heading from London to Edinburgh. You have got the world's greatest detective, Sherlock Holmes, and his buddy Dr. Watson right there with you. Their job is simple: protect a massive, expensive diamond called the Star of Rhodesia. But things go south fast. Within an hour, a murder happens and the diamond vanishes. Since the train is moving, the killer is trapped in the car with everyone else. It feels like a classic game of Clue where you are trying to figure out which passenger is lying and who is actually the thief. 

What really works here is the fast pace and the great chemistry between the leads. The mystery keeps you guessing, and the tight setting makes every conversation feel important. While some of the acting feels a bit stiff by today's standards, it adds to that old-school charm. If you love a good whodunit, you should definitely check this out. You can find it as a rental on Apple TV or, if you love physical media, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: Holmes figures out that the crime was a clever trick. The killer used a secret way to move through the train to hide their tracks. After questioning the passengers and spotting a small clue they missed, Holmes reveals the thief's true identity. The stolen diamond is recovered just in time. The movie ends with the criminal being arrested and Watson praising Holmes for solving the case while the train reaches its stop.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old detective stories and murder mysteries.
